T h e Environmental Control e n d Lile Support
System (ECLSS) for the Space Station Freedom
has been in development at the Marshall Space
Flight Center (MSFC) since the mid- 1980's and,
when operational in the mid- 1 9 9 0 ' ~will he the
most advanced ECLSS ever flown. In order t o
minimize expendables a n d the amounts of water
and gases required I'or resupply, the water and air
will be recycled to an extent unprecedented in
space flight. Trace contaminants and microorgan-
isms are of greater concern than o n previous, short-
e r duration, missions d u e to longer periods of expo-
sure, a n d must be monitored a n d controlled to
extremely low levels. With a design lifetime of 30
years, it i s imperative that F r e e d o m ' s ECLSS he
highly reliable, a s autonomous as feasible, and easi-
ly maintainahle.
Alternative technologies for performing the
ECLS functions are being evaluated a n d the tech-
nologies most suitable for use ahoarcl Freedom are
being selected after extensive testing, including
both independent subsystem testing :ind integrated
system testing. Much has been learned abuut each
of the technologies evaluated, in terms of individu-
al suhsystem perlormance and interaction with oth-
e r subsystems.
T h e knowledge gained during clevelupment o f
Freedum's ECLSS will be valuable for future hu-
m a n space exploration missions as well. As mis-
sions increase in duration a n d distance from Earth,
the requirements become even more demanding.
T h e ECLSS of future missions will build upon
Freedom's which has to deal with many of the same
concerns.' 2 3
